page: Amazon Web Services m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Xen hypervisor and an x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.4 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the m4.2xlarge exhibits moderate multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score register in the average range, while single-core metrics from Geekbench and stress-ng fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains stable, with read and write tests for large blocks scoring in the middle 50%. However, specialized tasks such as database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are categorized as weak, reflecting the older generation of the underlying hardware.

Given its hardware profile, the m4.2xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads that require a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio but do not demand high single-thread performance or local storage. It can support basic multi-threaded applications, small-scale development environments, and moderate background processing tasks. The lack of local NVMe storage and the 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth represent significant tradeoffs for I/O-intensive applications, making it less optimal for high-throughput databases or real-time data streaming.
